status: v4, revised 2026-09-05 against the CTO's three sign-off clarifications; the approval row in ../../APPROVALS.md names this revision's commit id (D44)
promise: your words and your files, nothing else (CTO, 2026-09-05)

unit.name: logical usage unit
unit.not_a_byte: A Unicode scalar is not a byte. The two contributors are measured in different quantities - characters and bytes - and convert into the allowance at the same 1:1 rate, so the shared unit is named for what it is rather than for either half. Earlier revisions called it a 'logical byte'; the rename changed no number.
unit.printed_sentence: For your storage allowance, each character of writing counts as one byte, and files count by their original file size.
unit.generosity_note: Deliberately generous for non-Latin scripts: a Japanese character occupies three bytes of our storage and counts as one, so those customers fit more real content into 100 GB, not less. This is intended, not a rounding to be reconciled later.
unit.decimal: 100 GB = 100,000,000,000 decimal (D78) - the unit Backblaze bills in. Internal binary bounds are written GiB and never GB.
unit.printed_sentence_note: Replaced verbatim at v4. The earlier wording explained the text half and left the files half to inference.

constants_note: Two constants, both 1, one per contributor, so the conversion into the allowance is visible. NODE_UNIT, ATTRIBUTE_UNIT, MARK_RUN_UNIT, REFERENCE_UNIT, SCALAR_VALUE_UNIT and PROPERTY_UNIT were withdrawn by the CTO on 2026-09-05 (D79): structure is free.
charged_fields: ProjectedAttr.value where kind is text or url
free_fields: every other field of ProjectedNode and ProjectedAttr — identity, tree position, kind, block properties, marks, references, and values that are not words, including ProjectedAttr.role
text_unit: Unicode scalar values (characters), never UTF-8 bytes and never grapheme clusters — see logical-usage-v1.md section 2.2
files_unit: verified plaintext bytes, once per workspace per distinct dedup identity — see section 4
reading_the_inputs: A node object mirrors koru_projection::model::ProjectedNode. Any field not written takes its default: null for an option, false for done, an empty list for runs and attrs.
Nodes, runs, attributes and references appear in the inputs even though they are free, because a vector must show what was present and cost nothing — that is what makes a later re-pricing visible.
listing.trashed_at is the ADR-95 stamp on the manifest entry; durable=false means the document is no longer in the Cloud replica's durable document set.
Blob dedup identities are within-workspace identities derived from the workspace's WorkspaceBlobIdentityKey, never a plaintext BlobHash.

verified_plaintext_length_bytes is derived from the authenticated ciphertext envelope framing minus fixed versioned overhead (D40). Blob.size never appears in these vectors because it is never an input.

Case 21's input is parametric (document_count plus each_document) rather than enumerated, and carries configured_resource_limits plus an attempted_operation; its expected block has separate billing and resource_limit sections because they are separate mechanisms.

cases.description: A Cloud-enabled workspace with no documents and no files.
One document, two unformatted paragraphs, English (ASCII).
The same two-node shape as 02, written in Japanese. This is where the character-vs-byte decision becomes money.
Arabic, including the mixed-direction fixture line with its explicit bidi control characters.
A task with a bold phrase, a checked box, a date attribute and a text attribute. After the 2026-09-05 decisions this case is mostly a list of things that are free.
Document 02, flagged trashed_at in the workspace listing (ADR-95: a stamp on the manifest entry, content intact).
The same content as 02, but the second paragraph has been moved into the document's own trash subtree.
Two documents: one live, one permanently removed. Loro still holds the removed document's history.
A page with one image node referencing one durable file.
Two documents in one workspace referencing the same file.
The same file uploaded into two workspaces of one account.
The only document referencing a file is in the Trash.
An image pasted into an ordinary page, whose listing kind is 'page' rather than 'file'.
One node of one document will not read. The tolerant projection walk would log it and skip it.
A document whose schema version is newer than the server understands.
The same visible text in two Unicode spellings, one document each.
An account part-way through a migration to a hypothetical LogicalUsageV2. Two workspaces, one already shadow-recomputed. The case fixes what may be read and what may never be summed.
One account: an active workspace, a turned-off one, a deletion-pending one, and a purged one.
A document references a file whose upload never finalized, so Cloud holds no bytes for it.
A sprint board: 21 nodes, 20 typed attributes, 10 checked boxes, 5 dividers and 5 embeds — and twelve characters of writing.

A workspace of one million documents with no text at all, sitting exactly on the document-count resource limit. It costs the customer nothing and costs Koru a great deal. The case exists to prove that billing and resource limits are two mechanisms, not one: zero cost, and a clear refusal.
An account whose usage a version migration raises from 92 GB to 104 GB. The case fixes the number a durable receipt is refused against, and how that number comes back down.

field_names.documents_units: LU, counted from characters - must not say bytes
field_names.files_bytes: bytes - a file genuinely is a byte count, and each byte contributes one LU
field_names.logical_usage_units: LU - the sum, in units, because one of its halves is not bytes
field_names.note: The asymmetry is deliberate (contract 2.1), not an inconsistency to tidy.

resource_limits.note: Not billing rules. They never change a usage number and never enter the arithmetic. See contract 7.2.

v3_rename: The v3 unit rename changed no total. Every expected value below is the value v2 committed.

grandfathered_threshold.note: The number a durable receipt is refused against. Equal to the pool for every account never raised by a migration, so there is one rule and no special case. See contract 10.4.
grandfathered_threshold.written_at_migration: max(pool, post_migration_usage), inside the switch transaction
grandfathered_threshold.ratchet: max(pool, min(threshold, current_usage)) on every recomputation - non-increasing between migrations, floored at the pool
grandfathered_threshold.flagged: The ratchet is the one rule this contract supplies rather than records; contract 12.2 item L flags it for correction at sign-off.
